source_resources.title: Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques: Promising Directions From Cognitive and Educational Psychology
source_resources.author: John Dunlosky, Katherine A. Rawson, Elizabeth J. Marsh, Mitchell J. Nathan, Daniel T. Willingham
source_resources.version_or_verification_date: Psychological Science in the Public Interest, 2013 (Verified: 2026-10-30)
source_resources.license: Journal publisher copyright (all rights reserved) - lawful external linking only
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external citation of the publisher record; no text imported into curriculum materials.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Detailed comparative review rating practice testing and distributed practice as high-utility techniques while rating highlighting and rereading low-utility; anchors the retrieval, correction, and spaced-review design of Days 88-90.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Paywalled at SAGE; author-hosted preprints exist on university sites.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Curriculum restates the utility ratings and application conditions in original prose; every task remains runnable offline.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Pashler et al. Learning Styles: Concepts and Evidence
compared_candidates.license: Publisher copyright (originally Wiley; now SAGE Publications)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Important negative result on learning-styles matching but narrower scope; Dunlosky et al. rates a broader set of techniques directly usable for this curriculum.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Brown, Roediger & McDaniel: Make It Stick: The Science of Successful Learning
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Strong trade-book synthesis of the same evidence base; the peer-reviewed review is preferred for citation precision and technique-by-technique utility ratings.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Psychological Science in the Public Interest 14(1): 4-58; practice testing and distributed practice sections

source_resources.title: Python Standard Library: Built-in Exceptions
source_resources.author: Python Software Foundation
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external reference under PSF open documentation terms; no source text imported into curriculum content.
source_resources.prerequisites: Basic Python syntax from Study Days 01-09
source_resources.selection_rationale: Normative exception hierarchy used to justify the narrowest correct except clause and FileNotFoundError attributes such as filename and errno.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Hosted on python.org; requires internet access unless a local documentation bundle is installed.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The drill reproduces FileNotFoundError and ValueError locally, and help(ValueError) documents the hierarchy offline.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Beginner-friendly but non-normative; omits the OSError attributes and hierarchy precision the diagnosis drills require.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Python Tutorial: Classes and Error Handling chapters (non-exception view)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Broader class-oriented chapter; the dedicated exceptions reference is the tighter fit for reading and diagnosing concrete error types during debugging checks.

source_resources.title: CS231n: Backpropagation and Intuitions
source_resources.author: Andrej Karpathy / Stanford University
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external reference under open course license.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Modular local-gradient interpretation (gate operations: add, multiply, max) and gradient flow intuition.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Karpathy Hacker's Guide to Neural Networks
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Raw circuit view; CS231n notes are more structured with explicit gate derivations.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Fast.ai Practical Deep Learning for Coders
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Top-down approach; CS231n bottom-up modular view matches our first-principles curriculum.

source_resources.safe_fallback: Local gate definitions and circuit flow diagrams in the lesson provide full coverage.

source_resources.title: Pro Git, Second Edition
source_resources.author: Scott Chacon and Ben Straub
source_resources.permission_basis: Linking only; no book text reproduced in curriculum content; reuse limited to noncommercial references consistent with CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.
source_resources.prerequisites: Basic git status/log/diff vocabulary from earlier study days
source_resources.selection_rationale: Freely licensed reference for branching, merging, conflict resolution, and safe recovery vocabulary used on Day 14.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Readable free at git-scm.com; availability depends on the site staying online.
source_resources.safe_fallback: git help <command> and the Git manual pages ship with Git and cover the same commands offline; every required workflow is stated locally in the lesson.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Interactive but requires a GitHub account and an external service; disposable local repositories keep the exercise self-contained.
Vendor-owned prose with no permissive license; Pro Git covers the same ground under CC BY-NC-SA.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Chapter 3 Git Branching and Section 7.7 Reset Demystified

source_resources.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
source_resources.author: Shunyu Yao, Jeffrey Zhao, Dian Yu, Nan Du, Izhak Shafran, Karthik Narasimhan, Yuan Cao
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external technical citation and reference under open access repository terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Prompt engineering, token generation basics, and conversational interaction loops.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Foundational academic paper introducing the interleaved Thought-Action-Observation control loop in LLM agents, establishing formal interleaving of task reasoning and external tool execution.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Permanently accessible on arXiv.org open access repository.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Complete algorithmic step traces, state loop diagrams, and control loop pseudocode are self-contained in curriculum materials.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models (Wei et al. 2022)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Pure reasoning without environmental actions or external tool grounding; ReAct extends reasoning into an interactive environment action-observation loop.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: MRKL Systems: A modular, neuro-symbolic architecture that combines large language models, external knowledge sources and discrete reasoning (Karpas et al. 2022)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Early neuro-symbolic modular router concept; ReAct offers simpler, prompting-native action-observation loop dynamics suitable for standard API models.

source_resources.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
source_resources.author: Carlos E. Jimenez, John Yang, Alexander Wettig, Shunyu Yao, Kexin Pei, Ofir Press, Karthik R. Narasimhan
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic reference under arXiv open access terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Unit testing, issue descriptions, and repository evaluation vocabulary.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Defines the standard pattern this block teaches: a bounded issue statement paired with executable fail-to-pass tests as verifiable acceptance criteria for agent-produced changes.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The acceptance-criteria pattern is exercised locally through the Ticket 22 fixture scorer and the Ticket 24 regression exercise without external datasets.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: HumanEval: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Function-level synthesis benchmark; SWE-bench models the repository-scoped issue-to-diff workflow that this delivery block rehearses.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Multi-SWE-bench: A Multilingual Benchmark for Issue Resolving
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Extends issue resolution to multiple programming languages; the original Python-centric SWE-bench provides a cleaner pedagogical anchor.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 2.1 Benchmark Construction and Section 2.2 Task Formulation (FAIL_TO_PASS tests)

source_resources.title: Test-Enhanced Learning: Taking Memory Tests Improves Long-Term Retention
source_resources.author: Henry L. Roediger III, Jeffrey D. Karpicke
source_resources.license: Journal publisher copyright (all rights reserved) - lawful external linking only
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external citation of the publisher record; no text imported into curriculum materials.
source_resources.prerequisites: Basic understanding of study sessions, retention intervals, and experimental design vocabulary.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Foundational experimental evidence that retrieval practice (testing) outperforms repeated study for long-term retention; grounds the Day 88 AI-free retrieval checks in peer-reviewed learning science rather than folk advice.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Publisher page may be paywalled; author preprints and university repositories host lawful copies.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The curriculum restates the experimental design and effect sizes in original prose; every sealed task runs without the paper.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Cepeda et al. Distributed Practice in Verbal Recall Tasks: A Review and Quantitative Synthesis
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Strong meta-analytic coverage of spacing effects but addresses scheduling rather than the retrieval effect itself; retained as support for the Day 90 spaced-review schedule.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Karpicke & Roediger: The Critical Importance of Retrieval for Learning (Science 2008)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Equally foundational follow-up demonstrating repeated retrieval vs repeated study; the 2006 paper is cited as the standard first controlled demonstration.

source_resources.title: The Turing Way: A Handbook for Reproducible, Ethical and Collaborative Data Science
source_resources.author: The Turing Way Community
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external reference under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; only links and original explanations are used.
source_resources.prerequisites: Basic version control and command-line familiarity.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Community-maintained CC-BY handbook codifying reproducibility checklists (versioned code, environment capture, rerunnable commands); directly defines the Day 90 reproduction-verification and provenance-audit workflow.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Freely hosted online; Netlify mirror availability is not guaranteed offline.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The portfolio checklist and verification log schema are authored locally; reproduction commands run without the handbook.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Wilson et al. Good enough practices in scientific computing (PLOS CB 2017)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Concise practices paper; The Turing Way's maintained, checklist-driven coverage of environments and reproducibility is broader and kept current.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Sandve et al. Ten Simple Rules for Reproducible Computational Research (PLOS CB 2013)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Foundational rules list; The Turing Way expands the same rules into actionable checklists used verbatim for the Day 90 verification run.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Reproducible Research chapter: version control, testing, environment capture
